meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
That's a file history, Hale, not a conversation with Owen. Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first, so did you speak with Owen before you entered that zero?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

Students misquote plays from memory, Hale, and a wrong line is an error in an essay, not proof of anything else. I'm writing the line down and I'll search it myself. You also haven't answered whether you spoke to Owen before the zero.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing, including that nothing goes on his record. "If it holds up" is your word, so who decides that, and does the zero come off today?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room with the vice-principal present, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the zero withdrawn today, the terms in writing, an answer on who decides whether the rewrite holds up, and an answer on whether you spoke with Owen before entering the mark. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She finished at her fallback, having recognised procedure 4.4 and asked for it in writing, but she had not agreed to the rewrite and still wants the zero off today and nothing on his record; the private supervised rewrite is the fair outcome, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You cited 4.4 correctly and committed to it, which met her fallback demand about his record.
What cost ground: You never answered whether you spoke with Owen before entering the zero, which left her strongest procedural point standing.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history of late-night edits the night before the due date came close to that night, and that is why she shortened her answers and went straight to procedure, but it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When you described the version history, turn the screen toward her and answer directly whether you spoke with Owen first, so the evidence and your own process are both on the table.
